info.text:
In 2025, nearly 1 in 3 US adults had income that varied at least occasionally.

11% of all adults said that made bills hard to pay, up from about 9% in 2021 (Fed SHED).
A 2019 JPMorgan Chase Institute study found the typical family in its data (Chase accounts, 2013-2018) saw income move 36% month to month.
Three common approaches: baseline (lowest-month) budgeting, an income buffer, and percent-based allocation. Hypothetical example inside.

Sources: Federal Reserve, Economic Well-Being of U.S. Households in 2025 (May 2026); JPMorgan Chase Institute, Weathering Volatility 2.0 (Oct 2019).
News and education, not financial advice.
Follow @financeprostv for money explained simply.
